confirmed.summary: project_solid_edges emits over-top diffraction candidates with along-axis x outside [0, dp] (behind the source / beyond the receiver); upper_hull_select's monotone-chain precondition is violated, fabricating a phantom multi-edge barrier from a solid that isn't between S and R.
confirmed.detail: project_walls gates crossings to the S->R segment via t in [0,1] (line 681), so wall candidates always have x in [0,dp]. project_solid_edges only checks the EDGE parameter lam in [0,1] (line 725) and then pushes x = `along` = projection onto the S->R direction with NO [0,dp] bound (lines 733-734). A 3-D Obstacle::Solid (or gable/hip) whose plan footprint straddles the infinite S->R plan line but lies beyond R (or behind S) has roof/eave edges that cross the vertical S->R plane at along>dp (or <0). upper_hull_select (line 742) is a plain Andrew monotone chain that does NOT sort internally: build_geometry sorts candidates by x (line 910) but upper_hull_select then prepends S at x=0 and appends R at x=dp, so an out-of-range candidate makes the point sequence non-monotone and the resulting hull is wrong. The beyond-R edge is retained as an 'active' diffracting edge; path_lengths (line 784) then scores a path S->...->(edge beyond R)->R with an enormous delta_z, which abar_spectrum caps at 20/25 dB. Net: a solid that does not screen the S->R path adds up to ~25 dB of phantom attenuation, and can make `active` non-empty (returning Some(geometry)) even when there is no real screen at all. Fix: filter in project_solid_edges (e.g. `if !(-eps..=dp+eps).contains(&along) { continue; }`, mirroring project_walls' t gate), or drop candidates with x outside [source.x, receiver.x] inside upper_hull_select.
confirmed.failure_scenario: S=(0,0,2), R=(100,0,2), and one Obstacle::Solid box at e in [110,120], n in [-5,5], base 0, top 8 (a building directly behind the receiver, in line with the source - i.e. the standard facade-receiver geometry: receiver a few metres in front of a building, source across the field). The box top edges cross the vertical plane at x=110 and x=120 (>dp=100). upper_hull_select returns them as active edges; over_top.delta_z ~= 41 m -> Dz capped at 20/25 dB. The open S->R path is scored as if ~20-25 dB screened -> receiver level UNDER-predicted by up to ~25 dB (non-conservative). Symmetric failure for a solid behind the source (along<0). Escapes the test suite because case_20 places its solids between S and R (along in [5,15] within [0,20]).
confirmed.fix_sketch: In project_solid_edges, after computing `along`, skip when along is outside [0, dp] (mirror project_walls' t in [0,1] gate); or filter candidates to [source.x, receiver.x] in upper_hull_select.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED real and critical. project_solid_edges (solver/crates/iso9613-core/src/iso9613/barrier/path.rs:733-734) pushes over-top candidates at x=`along` (the raw S→R plan projection) with no [0,dp] bound, unlike project_walls which gates its crossings to the S→R segment via t∈[0,1] (line 681). It only requires lam∈[0,1] (line 725), i.e. the edge crosses the INFINITE vertical plane. upper_hull_select (742-780) does not sort internally; build_geometry sorts candidates by x (910) then brackets them with S at x=0 (750) and R at x=dp (754), so a candidate with along>dp makes the sequence non-monotone and Andrew's monotone chain yields a wrong hull. I hand-traced the cited scenario S=(0,0,2), R=(100,0,2), Solid box e∈[110,120] n∈[-5,5] z∈[0,8]: the two top edges crossing the vertical plane give candidates {x:110,z:8},{x:120,z:8} (both >dp=100); the hull becomes [S,(110,8),(120,8),R] so active=[{110,8},{120,8}] (non-empty ⇒ build_geometry returns Some), and path_lengths gives delta_z≈41 m. abar_spectrum then computes dz_uncapped≈34 dB capped at 25 dB (diffraction.rs:117-126), subtracted at standards/mod.rs:138. I checked the lateral-path rescue hypothesis and refuted it: the solid's lateral_plane_hull folds R into the middle of the sorted supports identically, so both lateral paths also come out with delta_z≈40.7 (screening, not open) — no energy-sum cancellation; net Abar≈24-25 dB. Reachability confirmed: Obstacle::Solid is a public serializable variant (scene/mod.rs:198), validate() imposes no positional gate (572-582), and barriers() feeds the raw edges to evaluate_general for every source-receiver pair (905/941/1154) with no culling. Building footprints are immune (their over-top uses gated project_walls → empty over-top beyond R → geometry None → laterals never scored), so the un-gated Solid over-top emission is the sole trigger. The scenario is a standard facade-receiver / noise-map geometry (a building behind the receiver, or symmetrically behind the source with along<0), producing up to ~25 dB of phantom, non-conservative attenuation. Severity critical: wrong results in realistic scenes, reachable through the typed/JSON/Session public API.

confirmed.summary: Heightfield.heights vector length is never validated against nx*ny, so a raster terrain with a short heights array panics with an index-out-of-bounds through the public API.
confirmed.detail: `Heightfield::node` does `self.heights[iy * self.nx + ix]` with no bounds relationship enforced. `height_at` only guards `nx==0 || ny==0 || spacing<=0`; it never checks `heights.len() == nx*ny`. Critically, `Scene::validate()` (scene/mod.rs:477-587) does NOT inspect `scene.terrain` at all — not the array length, not finiteness. `Terrain::Heightfield` is a public, serde-deserializable field, so a caller (typed Scene, solve_json, Session, py, wasm) can supply nx/ny that exceed heights.len(). The first `Terrain::profile_edges`/`mean_height` -> `height_at` -> `node` call then indexes past the end and panics, aborting the solve (in wasm this unwinds to a JS trap). Separately, `heights` values are also never finiteness-checked, so a NaN/Inf cell silently propagates a non-finite `z` into the diffraction edge and hence a non-finite Lp.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Scene{schema_version:1, standard:Iso9613_2_2024, atmosphere:default, ground:{default_g:0.5}, terrain:Some(Heightfield{origin:[0,0], spacing:1.0, nx:10, ny:10, heights:vec![0.0]}), sources:[{id:"s",kind:General,position:[0,0,10],height_agl:10,lw:[100;10]}], receivers:[{id:"r",position:[50,0,1.5],height_agl:1.5}], ...}. validate() passes (terrain untouched). solve() -> compute -> terrain.profile_edges -> Heightfield::profile_edges -> height_at(x,y) -> node(ix,iy)=heights[iy*10+ix], which reaches heights[99] on a length-1 Vec -> panic: index out of bounds. Any nx*ny > heights.len() (including heights empty) triggers it.
confirmed.fix_sketch: In validate(), for Terrain::Heightfield reject `heights.len() != nx*ny`, `spacing` non-finite/<=0, and any non-finite height; or make `node` bounds-check and return a sentinel.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed. `Heightfield::node` (terrain.rs:31) indexes `self.heights[iy*self.nx + ix]` with no invariant tying `heights.len()` to `nx*ny`. `height_at` (terrain.rs:37) guards only `nx==0||ny==0||spacing<=0`, then clamps `ix,iy` into `[0,nx-1]/[0,ny-1]` and calls `node` up to index `nx*ny-1`, so any `heights.len() < nx*ny` (including empty) panics with index-out-of-bounds. `Heightfield` (terrain.rs:20-27) is a plain pub-field struct with a derived `Deserialize` — no smart constructor, custom deserialize, or length invariant anywhere (verified by Grep across all crates). Critically, `Scene::validate()` (scene/mod.rs:477-587) never inspects `scene.terrain` at all, even though it validates the identical index-range class for `Obstacle::Solid` edges at lines 576-578 — so the terrain gap is a real omission. The panic is reachable through every public entry point: `solve` (846-849) and `Session::solve` (1271-1280) both call `validate()` (which passes) then reach the compute closure at scene/mod.rs:893-897, which unconditionally calls `terrain.profile_edges` → `height_at` → `node`; `solve_json` (1230-1234, the documented FFI seam) deserializes the inconsistent heightfield from JSON and calls `solve`; the py binding wraps `solve_json` (iso9613-py/src/lib.rs:28). The reviewer's failure scenario (nx=ny=10, heights=vec![0.0], S=[0,0,10], R=[50,0,1.5]) reaches `height_at` on the first interior sample and indexes past a length-1 Vec. A realistic off-by-one in nx/ny from a truncated DEM tile, or an empty heights array, triggers the same hard panic instead of the clean SceneError the validate() contract promises. Refuted on none of the four axes; matches the rubric's critical definition (panic reachable through the public API — Scene JSON / typed API / Session / solve_json / py). The secondary claim (no finiteness check on heights letting a NaN/Inf cell propagate a non-finite z) is also correct but subordinate to the panic.

confirmed.summary: Session mutators commit the edit to self.scene BEFORE validate() runs, so a rejected edit leaves the Session corrupted and the next solve() panics.
confirmed.detail: set_source_lw stores `src.lw = lw` (1310) then calls `self.scene.validate()?` (1311). On failure the `?` returns Err but the bad-length lw is already in the cached scene and self.system was never reassigned. The documented invariant (lines 1240-1243: 'Session holds a VALIDATED scene ... solve is always safe to call') is now false: solve_cached calls BandSpectrum::from_iter(self.system, src.lw) whose assert_eq! (spectrum.rs:166) panics on the length mismatch. set_receivers (1299), set_obstacles (1322) and update() (1329) share the same commit-before-validate pattern (set_receivers instead yields silent NaN receivers; set_obstacles leaves self.walls stale vs the new obstacles).
confirmed.failure_scenario: session = Session::new(scene_with_one_10band_source). `let e = session.set_source_lw("s1", vec![1.0;7])` returns Err(BadLwLength) but scene.sources[0].lw is now 7-long and self.system stays Octave(10). Caller logs e and continues; next session.solve() hits BandSpectrum::from_iter(Octave,7-elem) -> assert panics 'length 7 doesn't match 10 bands'. Same via switching one source of a multi-source octave scene to 31 bands (MixedBandSystems). Through the PyO3 Session (crates/iso9613-py/src/lib.rs:72) this surfaces as a pyo3 PanicException after a caught ValueError.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Validate the candidate value first (or clone-validate-then-commit) so a rejected mutation leaves scene, system and the cached decomposition untouched.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed reachable panic through the public API. In scene/mod.rs:1310 `set_source_lw` writes `src.lw = lw` into the cached `self.scene` BEFORE calling `self.scene.validate()?` (1311). For a wrong-band-count vector (e.g. len 7, or len 31 in a multi-source octave scene → MixedBandSystems), validate returns Err at mod.rs:502-506 via `band_system_for` (463-468), the `?` propagates, and `self.system` is left at the old value — poisoning the Session (scene source lw len 7, system=Octave/10). `Session::solve` (1271) is infallible (`-> Results`) and performs no re-validation; it calls solve_cached (855) whose compute closure runs `BandSpectrum::from_iter(system, src.lw…)` at mod.rs:884, tripping `assert_eq!(bands.len(), system.n_bands())` at spectrum.rs:166 → panic. Session and the three methods are `pub` (consumed by iso9613-py/src/lib.rs:21); through PyO3 the rejected edit is a catchable ValueError (py lib.rs:72) but the next `solve()` (py lib.rs:60) becomes an uncatchable PanicException. set_receivers (1299), set_obstacles (1322) and update (1329) share the same commit-before-validate pattern (set_receivers → NaN outputs; set_obstacles → scene.obstacles new but self.walls/solids stale = silently wrong results). Refutations fail: no guard on the solve path, the trigger is a routine wrong-length spectrum rather than exotic geometry, and the mutator's `Result` return type plus the doc-comment invariant (mod.rs:1242-1243, "solve is always safe to call") actively invite the non-fatal error handling that leads to the crash. I raise the reviewer's self-rated "major" to critical because the severity rubric explicitly classifies a panic reachable through the public Session/py API as critical, and here it surfaces on an infallible, documented-safe method with no bad input at its own call site and no error channel to defend against it.

confirmed.summary: A receiver coincident with a source (d=0) makes Adiv = 20*log10(0)+11 = -inf, so every per-band Lp becomes +inf with no error reported.
confirmed.detail: `adiv` computes `20.0 * d.log10() + 11.0` where `d` is the 3-D source->receiver distance, with no lower floor. When d==0 (source and receiver at the same point) log10(0) = -inf, so `evaluate_general` (standards/mod.rs:138) computes `out.bands[b] = lw - (-inf) - aatm - agr - abar = +inf` for every band (aatm=0 since d_km=0; agr/abar finite; cmet=0 since dp<=0). The result is not rejected: `SourceContribution.bands` are all +inf and `total_dba` is silently masked to None by the `is_finite` guard at scene/mod.rs:1191. Through solve_json these +inf bands serialize as JSON `null`, so a host sees null levels with no error. (If additionally h_s=h_r=0, agr's Kgeo is 0/0 = NaN and the band becomes NaN instead.) This is the canonical d=0->Adiv degeneracy; it is reachable through every public entry point.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Scene with sources:[{position:[0,0,5],height_agl:5,lw:[100;10]}] and receivers:[{position:[0,0,5],height_agl:5}] (receiver placed exactly on the source — a plausible grid slip where the grid cell overlaps a source). solve() returns per_receiver[0].per_source[0].bands = [+inf;10] and total_dba = None, with Ok(...) and no SceneError.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Floor the distance in adiv (e.g. `d.max(d0)` with d0=1 m) or return SceneError/skip the pair when d < ~1e-3 m; alternatively clamp Adiv to a finite maximum.

verdict.reasoning: Verified end-to-end and the defect is genuine. divergence.rs:15-16 computes `adiv = 20·d.log10() + 11` with `d = receiver.sub(source).length()` and no floor; at exact source/receiver coincidence `d = sqrt(0) = 0` (units.rs:20-26) and `(0.0f64).log10() = -inf`, so `adiv = -inf`. All other terms stay finite: aatm = alpha·(d/1000) = 0 (atmosphere.rs:89-97); Agr = 0 for the 2024 KgeoWrap because `kgeo = (0+0)/(0+h_sum²)=0` makes `arg=1.0` (ground/general.rs:63,82-88), and finite for 1996 Sum since `a_prime(5,0)=1.5` (functions.rs:19-27); cmet = 0 because dp=0 (meteorology.rs:16). Thus standards/mod.rs:138 yields `out.bands[b] = 100 − (−inf) − 0 − 0 − 0 = +inf` for every band, stored into SourceContribution.bands at scene/mod.rs:1121 (cmet=0). The result is silently non-finite: scene/mod.rs:1183-1191 energy-sums `10^(0.1·inf)=+inf`, `a_weighted_total()` returns +inf, and the `is_finite()` guard maps `total_dba` to None while returning Ok. Reachability is confirmed — validate() (scene/mod.rs:477-587) has no source≠receiver check, so the failure scenario passes validation and flows through solve()/Session/solve_json alike; solve_json serializes the +inf bands as JSON `null`, so a host gets null levels and a null total with NO SceneError. This is a real silent-misleading trap (and with multiple sources, one coincident source nulls the entire receiver's total, masking all other valid contributions). I downgrade critical→major: it is not a panic/crash/non-termination, and exact 3-D coincidence of a source and receiver is a plausible degenerate edge case (a grid slip), not a realistic scene — squarely the major rubric ("wrong results in plausible edge cases / API traps that silently mislead").

confirmed.summary: cluster_lateral_paths pools EVERY convex footprint in the scene into a single lateral-plane hull; a building farther off the S->R axis rides the upper hull and evicts a nearer screening building's genuine around-the-side path, dropping real lateral energy.
confirmed.detail: build_geometry passes all scene footprints (evaluate_general standards/mod.rs:129; solve_cached passes every Obstacle::Building), and cluster_lateral_paths (lines 185-198) collects ALL convex footprints and hands them to one convex_cluster_paths -> lateral_plane_hull call (line 197 -> 261), pooling every building's edges. lateral_plane_hull builds one upper hull per side over the pooled supports, keeping the maximum-t (farthest perpendicular offset) corners. When source and receiver are at equal height (very common), the lateral plane is horizontal at z=zs, so EVERY building whose posts span that height contributes supports. A second building farther from the S->R line (larger t) therefore dominates the upper hull and pops the nearer screening building's low-t corners: the returned lateral wraps the FAR building (huge delta_z, negligible energy under the Eq-25 combine in abar_spectrum) and the near building's real low-delta_z side path is discarded. Dropping a lateral energy term raises Abar and LOWERS the predicted level (non-conservative). Pooling is correct only for a genuine tight cluster (T16/T17, all buildings between S and R inside one convex hull); it is applied scene-wide with no proximity grouping. Note the asymmetry: solids are wrapped per-solid (lines 928-930), so the same two buildings modelled as Obstacle::Solid vs Obstacle::Building yield different laterals.
confirmed.failure_scenario: S=(0,0,2), R=(40,0,2); Building A footprint [10,15]x[-2.5,2.5] height 6 straddling the S->R line (screens over-top); Building B footprint [18,23]x[10,15] height 10 off to the +n side (t~10-15, does not cross S->R). On the +n side the pooled upper hull wraps B's corners (t~15) and pops A's corners (t~2.5), so A's around-the-side diffraction on that side is lost -> Abar over-estimated -> receiver level under-predicted by up to a few dB. Any two-building scene at equal S/R heights is affected.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Group footprints by proximity/relevance to the S->R corridor before pooling (only cluster buildings the S->R segment actually interacts with), or wrap each footprint separately like solids and energy-combine, rather than one scene-wide convex hull.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed after failing every refutation. Reachability is unconditional: scene/mod.rs:639 pushes every Obstacle::Building into footprints with no corridor/proximity filter; build_geometry (path.rs:894) forwards the whole slice to cluster_lateral_paths (path.rs:927), which pools ALL convex footprints into one convex_cluster_paths -> lateral_plane_hull call (path.rs:196-261). lateral_plane_hull (path.rs:313-341) builds a single max-t upper hull per side and emits only one path per side; for equal-height S/R the lateral plane is horizontal (u2=(0,1,0), so t = plan n), so a farther building's large-t corners dominate the hull and pop a nearer screening building's low-t corners. I hand-verified the cited scenario at 500 Hz: the true +n path around building A (delta_z~0.43 m, ~11.9 dB, energy term ~0.065) is replaced by the pooled wrap around building B (delta_z~11.1 m, ~25.2 dB, term ~0.003), and abar_spectrum (barrier/mod.rs:96-114) energy-sums these, so the dominant near lateral is lost -> combined Dz rises from ~8.0 to ~10.2 dB, i.e. ~2.2 dB non-conservative UNDER-prediction of the receiver level, with the -n lateral and over-top unaffected. No recovery path exists: buildings emit only FootprintLateral, never LateralEdge, so select_lateral (path.rs:870) cannot rescue A's side path, and over-top is vertical-plane only. The asymmetry clinches it: solids are wrapped per-solid (path.rs:928-929), so the identical two obstacles as Solid vs Building give different laterals, confirming per-obstacle wrapping is the intended-correct behaviour and scene-wide pooling is the defect; pooling also violates the code's own stated most-transmitting-per-side rule (barrier/mod.rs:10) by keeping the least-transmitting far path. Severity major rather than critical because the error is silent and non-conservative in ordinary multi-building scenes but bounded to one corrupted lateral term (~2 dB in the two-building case) and requires the far building to sit on the same lateral side as a materially-leaking nearer building; it can compound in both-sides/3-building configurations.

confirmed.summary: Simplified-method mean height divides the profile area F by the 3-D slant source-receiver distance instead of the ground-projected base-point distance dg mandated by ISO 9613-2:2024 Eq 14 / Fig 5.
confirmed.detail: The standard defines hm = F/dg (2024 text line 983), where dg is 'the distance between the base points of source and receiver' (line 992) — i.e. the ground-projected/horizontal distance, excluding the source and receiver heights. mean_height() instead computes d = sqrt(dp^2 + (rz-sz)^2) at line 63 (the full 3-D slant distance, which includes the source/receiver elevations) and returns f/d at line 78. Since dp/d <= 1, hm is systematically underestimated by the factor dp/d. That feeds ground::simplified::agr where Agr = 4.8 - (2*hm/d)*(17 + 300/d): a too-small hm makes the subtracted term smaller and Agr larger, i.e. TOO MUCH ground attenuation and an under-predicted (non-conservative) receiver level. It is also internally inconsistent: over a perfectly flat Heightfield mean_height returns (hS+hR)/2 * (dp/d), which disagrees with the analytic hm_flat = (hS+hR)/2 used on the no-terrain path (the correct hm = F/dp reproduces hm_flat exactly). Note the 2024 change-list (line 189) also flags that the hm definition was modified vs 1996, so a single divisor cannot be exactly right for both editions, but F/d is wrong for the 2024 edition regardless. Fix: divide F by dp (the ground-projected distance), not the slant d.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Settings.ground_method = Simplified with a terrain Heightfield present and a non-trivial source/receiver height difference. E.g. dp = 50 m with a 40 m absolute height difference gives d ~ 64 m, so hm is ~22% low; where Agr lies between 0 and 4.8 dB this shifts Agr by several tenths of a dB (well beyond the project's own +/-0.05 dB bar) in the non-conservative direction. In the near-vertical limit (dp = 10 m, dz = 100 m) hm is underestimated by ~90%.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Return `f / dp` (and guard on dp, not d, in the degenerate check) so mean_height uses the base-point/ground-projected distance dg per Eq 14 / Fig 5; this also makes a flat Heightfield reproduce hm_flat.

verdict.reasoning: Verified against the primary source. ISO 9613-2:2024 (scratchpad iso2024.txt lines 983 & 992) states hm = F/dg with dg = "the distance between the base points of source and receiver" (ground-projected/horizontal), while d in Eq 14 is the slant source-receiver distance (line 982); the change-list (line 189) explicitly flags the hm definition as modified vs 1996. terrain.rs:63 computes d = sqrt(dp^2 + (rz-sz)^2) (slant) and line 78 returns f/d, so hm is divided by the slant distance rather than dg. F itself (lines 74-77, integral of vertical gap over horizontal dx) is the correct vertical-plane area, so only the divisor is wrong; the result is systematically low by the factor dp/d = cos(inclination), which makes the subtracted term in Agr = 4.8 - (2hm/d)(17+300/d) smaller, Agr larger, and the receiver level under-predicted (non-conservative). The path is reachable and not edition-guarded: GroundMethod::Simplified, Terrain::Heightfield, and the Iso2024 edition are all public; EditionSpec (standards/mod.rs:30-47) parameterizes only ground and barrier, and Iso2024 runs the same evaluate_general where hm_override (=F/slant-d, scene/mod.rs:900) feeds agr(hm, d) (standards/mod.rs:116-119) with no compensating correction. Worked example: ground rising 15 m over dp=50 m (~17deg inclination) with source and receiver 3 m above grade gives hm_true=3 vs hm_code=2.874, ~0.11 dB of spurious extra attenuation; a 39deg slope gives ~0.45 dB — both beyond the project's own +/-0.05 dB bar and in the non-conservative direction. The error is clamp-masked when hm is large (flat ground with tall S/R), which is why the mainline is unaffected, so severity is major (wrong results in a plausible Simplified-method + sloped-terrain edge case and a genuine 2024 conformance defect) rather than critical. Fix is hm = F/dp (keep slant d only inside the Agr formula), which also reconciles a flat Heightfield with hm_flat=(hS+hR)/2.

confirmed.summary: Higher-order Fresnel size gate computes the incidence angle from the ORIGINAL source for every reflector in the chain, instead of from the previous bounce point.
confirmed.detail: `reflect_chain` validates Eq 26/27 per reflector by calling `fresnel_valid(&refl, facade, source, lambda)` with the function-parameter `source` for ALL reflectors i=0..k-1. Inside `fresnel_valid` the incidence angles are derived from `source.sub(p)` (line 310). For a reflector i>=1 the incident ray at P_i actually arrives from the previous reflection point P_{i-1} (available here as `nodes[i]`), not from the original source. The bent leg lengths dSO/dOR passed in ARE correct; only the angle-of-incidence (alpha_a, alpha_h) and therefore leff=min(a·cos alpha_a, h·cos alpha_h) are wrong for the 2nd and higher bounces. This mis-computes leff and flips the per-band Fresnel decision (band included vs neglected) for every reflector after the first, even in the canonical parallel-wall canyon the feature targets (source->P_1 direction differs from P_0->P_1 direction whenever the source is not on the wall).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Two finite hard reflectors (alpha=0), e.g. building facades ~15 m wide forming a canyon, with max_reflection_order>=2, a General source and receiver between them. For the sequence [A,B] the 2nd bounce (reflector B) is gated using the source->P_B direction rather than the true P_A->P_B direction; at high-frequency bands (small lambda, near the leff threshold) this includes or excludes bands incorrectly, adding or dropping reflected energy in the 1-4 kHz region and shifting the A-weighted total. Fix: pass `nodes[i]` (source for i=0, points[i-1] otherwise) as the incidence origin instead of `source`.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed real. In reflect_chain (solver/crates/iso9613-core/src/iso9613/reflection.rs) the per-reflector Fresnel loop at lines 132-142 calls fresnel_valid(&refl, facade, source, lambda) at line 138 with the function parameter `source` (the original S) for every reflector i; `source` is never reassigned. Inside fresnel_valid, line 310 `let sp = source.sub(p)` (p = points[i]) and lines 313-316 derive cos_ah, cos_aa and leff = min(a·cos_aa, h·cos_ah) from that direction. For reflector i>=1 the incident ray physically arrives from points[i-1] (= nodes[i]), not from S, so the angle of incidence and therefore leff are wrong. fresnel_valid does not use refl.image_source and the dso/dor bent lengths passed in are correct, so the incidence origin is the sole error — exactly as claimed. ISO 9613-2:2024 confirms this is a defect: §7.5.2 defines αa/αh as the angle of incidence at the reflection point (iso2024.txt:1354, 1365), and §7.5.3 (lines 1427-1429) restricts the bent-path rule to *the lengths* dS,O/dO,R only ('validated for each reflector separately … even if these are bent at other reflectors'), leaving the angle a local per-bounce property (segment P_{i-1}→P_i). Reachable through the public API: scene/mod.rs:1015-1030 invokes reflect_chain with the source when max_reflection_order>=2 and >=2 reflectors for a General source — the documented street-canyon feature. Magnitude is non-trivial: in a canonical parallel canyon (walls y=0/y=10, S=(0,4), R=(30,6)) the true plan-incidence cosine at reflector 1 is 0.514 but the code computes 0.249 from S→P_1, a ~2× error in leff and ~4× in the Fresnel threshold, enough to flip per-band validity for ~15 m facades (e.g. 250-500 Hz), adding/dropping reflected energy for all bounces after the first. Severity is major rather than critical because the affected contribution is a secondary, opt-in (max_reflection_order>=2) energy-summed reflected path and only near-threshold bands flip, bounding the net A-weighted total error. The finding's proposed fix (pass nodes[i]: S for i=0, points[i-1] otherwise) is correct.

confirmed.summary: reflection_sequences enumerates all no-immediate-repeat sequences up to max_reflection_order with no upper bound, so a large order with >=3 reflectors allocates exponentially many Vecs and hangs/OOMs.
confirmed.detail: `max_reflection_order` is a serde-deserializable u32 with only `.max(1)` applied (scene/mod.rs:1014); there is no upper clamp. `reflection_sequences(m, order)` materialises every sequence of length 2..=order with no immediate repeat into `out` before any evaluation — count ~ sum_{k=2}^{order} m*(m-1)^(k-1). For m>=3 this is exponential in order: with 3 reflectors and order=25 it is ~5e7 Vecs (multi-GB), and order=30 is ~1.6e9 (certain OOM), effectively non-terminating. It is gated only by `max_order>=2 && reflectors>=2`, so an ordinary scene with 3 facades plus a large order value reaches it via the public API (solve/solve_json/Session).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Scene with reflectors:[R1,R2,R3] (any three valid facades), settings.max_reflection_order = 30, one source, one receiver, general kind. solve() -> reflection_sequences(3, 30) builds ~3*2^29 Vec<usize> into `out` -> multi-GB allocation, process hangs / is OOM-killed before returning.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Clamp max_reflection_order to a small ceiling (e.g. <=4) in validate(), and/or generate sequences lazily/iteratively with a hard cap on the number produced.

confirmed.summary: select_lateral keeps the global smallest-delta_z lateral edge per side across ALL thin-wall ends in the scene, so a non-screening wall's end near the S->R line can supplant the actually-screening wall's end.

Same class of scene-wide pooling as the footprint bug, with no per-obstacle relevance gate. (The side==0 tie sending an on-line edge to best_left is benign - at most one degenerate edge.) ISO 9613-2:2024 §7.5.2 requires the Formula (3)/(5) attenuation terms — including Abar — to be determined along the reflected propagation path (1996 §7.5 equivalent), so the omission is a genuine non-conformity, and the README advertises reflections as complete with no caveat. However, the finding's exemplar failure_scenario is wrong: Obstacle::Building decomposes into BOTH walls and a footprint (scene/mod.rs:623-644), and walls ARE passed (line 991), so a flat-roof building DOES screen the reflected ray over the top at up to the 20/25 dB cap; omitting footprints only drops energy-ADDING lateral wraps (abar_spectrum energy-sums laterals, barrier/mod.rs:103-114), which UNDER-predicts that reflected contribution — the opposite of the claimed one-directional over-prediction. The genuinely unscreened classes are terrain ridges (terrain_edges sampled only for the S→R profile, scene/mod.rs:893-897) and Obstacle::Solid, which decomposes ONLY into solids (scene/mod.rs:645-656) — and the gable/hip pitched-roof building constructors return Obstacle::Solid (scene/mod.rs:250), so in scenes modelling houses with pitched roofs plus a reflecting facade, reflected paths pass through intervening buildings with zero attenuation. Where the direct path is itself screened (exactly when reflections matter), the receiver total can be over-predicted by ~10-20 dB; with an unscreened direct path the spurious gain is bounded near 3 dB. Reachable through plain Scene JSON with no validation gate. Corrected severity major (wrong results in plausible edge cases, silently misleading), not critical (typical scenes keep a correctly-computed dominant direct path; large errors need the screened-direct + blocked-reflection conjunction) and not minor (it is a numeric correctness defect, not robustness/perf). The fix for footprints/solids is cheap (they are world-coordinate inputs projected per pair inside build_geometry, so passing them is geometrically valid for image→R); only terrain edges need recomputation along the reflected path.

confirmed.summary: Each Obstacle::Solid is wrapped for lateral (around-the-side) diffraction independently and is not pooled with Building footprints' convex cluster, so adjacent solids (or a solid next to a Building) don't share a taut string.
confirmed.detail: barriers() emits every solid as its own Solid3D (line 655); build_geometry (path.rs 928-930) then calls lateral_plane_hull per solid, while Building footprints are threaded together by cluster_lateral_paths (path.rs 927, convex_cluster_paths pools all footprint edges). Over-top diffraction IS pooled for solids (project_solid_edges into the shared upper hull, path.rs 907-909), so only the lateral term diverges. Result: a scene modelled with Obstacle::Solid gives a different lateral result than the identical geometry modelled with Obstacle::Building. Independent wrapping yields a shorter per-solid detour (less lateral attenuation -> typically over-prediction, conservative) and can route a lateral path through an adjacent, ignored solid. Documented only in a build_geometry code comment, not in the Obstacle::Solid API doc.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Two gable-roofed houses (Obstacle::gable -> Solid) side by side screening a receiver: each is wrapped alone, so the around-the-end path is shorter (less attenuation) than the same pair modelled as two flat Obstacle::Building, which cluster into one taut string. Impact bounded to geometries where lateral diffraction competes with over-top.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Feed solid edges into the same lateral-plane cluster construction as footprints (pool convex solids + buildings), or document the per-solid limitation on Obstacle::Solid.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by direct code reading. barriers() (solver/crates/iso9613-core/src/scene/mod.rs:645-656) emits each Obstacle::Solid as an independent Solid3D, and build_geometry (solver/crates/iso9613-core/src/iso9613/barrier/path.rs:928-930) calls lateral_plane_hull per solid, while Building footprints are pooled by cluster_lateral_paths (path.rs:927) via convex_cluster_paths (path.rs:244-262), which merges ALL convex footprints' edges into one taut-string construction; over-top IS pooled for solids (path.rs:907-910), so only lateral diverges. No occlusion check exists anywhere in the crate, so a per-solid wrap routes through an adjacent solid's volume. Because abar_spectrum energy-sums every lateral path (barrier/mod.rs:96-114) and a per-solid hull (subset of the pooled supports) always has Delta-z <= the pooled hull's, the Solid representation yields strictly less attenuation than the identical geometry as Buildings. Worked example: two adjacent 10 m houses (y in [-15,15], x in [30,40]) with S=(0,-1,2), R=(70,-1,2): house B's solo wrap around the shared y=0 boundary gives Dz_lat ~6 dB routed through house A, vs ~23 dB/side for the pooled cluster string — combined Abar ~5.6 dB vs ~15.7 dB, a ~10 dB representation-dependent divergence in a plausible row-of-houses scene. The single-obstacle equivalence test (tests/case_20_solid_and_pitched.rs:50-75) does not cover multi-obstacle scenes, and the Obstacle::Solid API doc (scene/mod.rs:187-197) omits the limitation while the Building doc (lines 178-181) steers pitched-roof users to Solid. Severity corrected minor -> major: this is a silent API trap producing wrong results (up to ~10 dB) in plausible scenes — the rubric's major bucket — though not critical because it requires multiple solids interacting in the lateral wrap with a lateral term competitive with over-top, and the error is uniformly conservative (over-predicts received noise).

confirmed.summary: reflection_sequences(m, max_order) is rebuilt for every (source, receiver) pair although it depends only on (m, max_order); max_reflection_order has no upper bound.
confirmed.detail: The higher-order block calls reflection_sequences() inside the per-receiver closure and the per-source loop, materialising the full O(m^order) sequence list each time even though it is identical for all sources/receivers. Settings.max_reflection_order (u32) is not capped in validate(). Most sequences are rejected cheaply by reflect_chain geometry, but sequence generation/allocation itself grows as ~m^order and is repeated N_receivers x N_sources times.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A scene with ~15 reflectors, max_reflection_order=4, 5 sources and a 3000-receiver grid rebuilds a ~15^4≈5e4-element Vec<Vec<usize>> ~15000 times; a larger order (e.g. m>=3, order>=8) makes the sequence enumeration explode and the solve effectively hang, reachable purely via scene JSON settings.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Hoist reflection_sequences out of the receiver/source loops (compute once per solve), and validate/cap max_reflection_order to a small maximum.

verdict.reasoning: Verified in solver/crates/iso9613-core/src/scene/mod.rs: reflection_sequences(scene.reflectors.len(), max_order) at line 1026 executes inside the per-source loop (line 882) inside the per-receiver compute closure (line 879), with loop-invariant arguments, so the full O(Σ m·(m−1)^(L−1)) sequence list is rebuilt and dropped for every (source, receiver) pair; Session (lines 1247+) caches only the obstacle decomposition, not sequences. validate() (lines 477–587) never checks Settings.max_reflection_order (u32, serde-default, line 268); line 1014 applies only .max(1), no ceiling, and the line-1015 gate needs just a General source plus 2 reflectors — reachable through solve_json (line 1230), Session, wasm and py. The claimed counts check out (m=15, order=4 → 44,310 ≈ ~5e4 per pair), though the finding's own m≥3/order≥8 example is weak (762 sequences); the real blow-up needs m≈10+ (m=10, order=8 → ~5.4e7 sequences, gigabytes per pair). The defect is actually worse than filed: reflection_sequences (lines 666–686) recurses to depth exactly max_order while accumulating O(depth²) memory, so scene JSON with max_reflection_order ≈ 1e5 and two reflectors causes an uncatchable stack-overflow/OOM abort, and plausible knob values (order 6–10, as commercial noise software permits) with ~10–12 reflectors make a multi-receiver solve effectively hang. Severity: the redundant rebuild alone is minor (per-sequence reflect_chain geometry dominates and is inherently per-pair), but the uncapped exponential parameter is an API trap producing hangs and process-killing aborts from plausible-to-pathological settings reachable purely via public JSON → major. Not critical: defaults (0→1) and documented/conformance usage (order 2) never enter the pathological region, and results are never silently wrong — the failure mode is resource exhaustion, not incorrect levels.

confirmed.summary: solve_parallel (and solve) run the multithreaded rayon core solve while holding the Python GIL — no py.allow_threads — so the whole interpreter is frozen for the duration of the solve.
confirmed.detail: The py crate builds iso9613-core with features=["parallel"] (crates/iso9613-py/Cargo.toml), so solve_par fans out over receivers on a rayon pool and solve()/solve_json use par_iter on rayon's global pool. Neither pyfunction takes Python<'_> nor calls allow_threads, so the calling thread holds the GIL for the entire (potentially multi-second) compute. The rayon workers themselves run, but every OTHER Python thread is blocked — directly defeating solve_par's stated purpose (core doc lines 1210-1215: 'leaves headroom so an interactive host ... stays responsive').
confirmed.failure_scenario: A Python web backend calls iso9613.solve_parallel(big_scene_json, 4) inside a request handler thread. For the whole solve of a large receiver grid, no other Python thread can run — all concurrent requests / async tasks / health checks stall until it returns. The plain solve() wrapper (line 27) has the same defect.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Parse the scene while holding the GIL, then wrap the compute: `py.allow_threads(|| scene::solve_par(&scene, max_threads))`, serialising results afterward. Copy scene_json to an owned String before releasing if needed.

verdict.reasoning: The finding is factually correct. Verified: crates/iso9613-py/Cargo.toml:15 enables core feature \"parallel\"; crates/iso9613-py/src/lib.rs has no pyfunction/pymethod taking Python<'_> and no py.allow_threads (grep confirms the only allow_threads/Python< hits are inside the compiled pyo3 rlib, not source). solve_parallel (line 34) calls scene::solve_par, which builds a private rayon pool and fans out via par_iter (scene/mod.rs:1202,1217-1222); solve (line 27) and Session::solve (line 60) route through solve_json/solve, which under the enabled \"parallel\" feature also par_iter on rayon's global pool. PyO3 mechanics: a #[pyfunction] taking &str (a borrow of a Python str, valid only while the GIL is held) that never calls allow_threads runs the entire compute with the GIL held, so the calling thread blocks every other Python thread for the whole solve. The rayon workers are native OS threads running pure physics with no Python callbacks, so the compute proceeds in parallel and returns CORRECT results and there is no deadlock — only other Python threads are starved. This directly undercuts the core doc's stated intent (scene/mod.rs:1213-1214: the thread budget \"leaves headroom so an interactive host (e.g. a web backend) stays responsive\"): a threaded Python backend that calls solve_parallel to stay responsive will instead freeze all other threads for the solve. HOWEVER, the reviewer's \"major\" is too high: this never produces wrong results, never panics, never corrupts cache state, and has zero impact on single-threaded callers or on the rayon parallelism itself (its actual promise). Impact is confined to host-thread responsiveness in a multithreaded Python host — a perf/responsiveness defect with practical impact plus mildly misleading behaviour, which is exactly the rubric's minor tier, not major. The fix (parse under the GIL, then py.allow_threads(|| scene::solve_par(&scene, max_threads)) before serializing) is correct. Genuine but minor.

confirmed.summary: When polygon_interior_point cannot find an interior point, concave_lateral_paths silently returns no lateral paths, dropping the building's around-the-side energy and under-predicting the level.
confirmed.detail: concave_lateral_paths needs an interior point to seed the homotopy cut ray; polygon_interior_point (lines 472-498) tries the centroid then a 19x19 bbox grid (361 samples). For a thin/sliver or deeply re-entrant concave footprint whose centroid is outside the polygon and whose interior misses every grid sample (interior area a small fraction of the bbox), it returns None and concave_lateral_paths returns Vec::new() (line 531). Because laterals only ADD energy in abar_spectrum's Eq-25 combine, dropping them raises Abar and lowers the predicted level (non-conservative), with no diagnostic.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A long narrow C/U-shaped concave building (bbox ~100x100 m but a ~1 m-wide wall run) between S and R: the centroid lands in the open courtyard (outside the polygon) and the coarse grid samples all miss the thin wall band -> polygon_interior_point returns None -> no lateral paths for that building -> its side diffraction is omitted -> receiver level under-predicted.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Fall back to a robust interior-point construction (e.g. a point just inside the polygon offset from an edge midpoint, or a denser/edge-seeded scan) instead of giving up and dropping the laterals.

verdict.reasoning: Verified real. polygon_interior_point (path.rs:472-498) uses a fixed 19x19 grid at fractions {1/20..19/20} of the bbox, so spacing = bbox/20 regardless of absolute scale. For a concave footprint whose solid bands are thinner than bbox/20, the centroid lands outside (path.rs:478-480 fails) and all 361 grid points fall in the open re-entrant region, so it returns None. I constructed an explicit valid case: a symmetric U 100x100 m with 4 m walls — grid y never enters the bottom bar (y<=4) and grid x never enters the arms (x<=4 or x>=96) -> None. On None, concave_lateral_paths returns Vec::new() (path.rs:531). A building's laterals come ONLY from this path: scene/mod.rs:639-643 emits exactly one FootprintLateral per building with no per-corner LateralEdge backup, and path.rs:190-193 routes every non-convex footprint exclusively to concave_lateral_paths, so the around-the-side energy is entirely dropped. Dropping laterals raises Abar and lowers the level (barrier/mod.rs:103-114: the Eq-25 energy sum makes combined < abar_top with laterals, = abar_top without), i.e. non-conservative under-prediction. Reachable through the public API: Scene::validate (scene/mod.rs:561-571) checks only >=3 vertices and finiteness — no convexity/thickness/self-intersection guard. Severity is minor, not major: the T18-style chunky concave buildings the code targets (wall/extent ~1/4-1/6) are caught by the grid, and for large buildings the dropped lateral is long and self-suppresses in the energy weighting; the bug requires an unusually thin-walled concave footprint (thickness < ~5% of extent). But the impact is not always cosmetic — laterals only combine with an active over-top screen (path.rs:918-920), so a tall thin-walled U with the source in the courtyard pocket can silently drop the DOMINANT least-attenuated path (many dB error), with no diagnostic. This matches the 'minor = robustness issue with practical impact, misleading behaviour' rubric.

confirmed.summary: Self-intersecting or degenerate (all-collinear / zero-area) building footprints are not rejected by Scene::validate and are silently mis-handled (is_convex misclassifies them), producing wrong laterals with no error.
confirmed.detail: Scene::validate only checks footprint.len()>=3 and finiteness (scene/mod.rs:561-571); it does not reject self-intersecting or degenerate polygons. is_convex (lines 203-224) tests only consecutive-turn sign consistency, so a self-intersecting 'bowtie' or a collinear footprint can be classified either way, and the convex (lateral_plane_hull) or concave (visibility-graph) lateral construction then produces geometrically meaningless - but non-crashing - lateral paths. The engine assumes simple polygons but nothing enforces it.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An Obstacle::Building with footprint [[0,0],[10,10],[10,0],[0,10]] (self-intersecting) passes validation; is_convex returns false -> concave_lateral_paths runs its visibility graph on a non-simple polygon -> the returned lateral paths are wrong, silently corrupting Abar with no error to the caller.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Reject self-intersecting / zero-area footprints in Scene::validate (simple-polygon test + minimum area), returning DegenerateBuilding.

verdict.reasoning: Mechanically the finding checks out. Scene::validate (solver/crates/iso9613-core/src/scene/mod.rs:561-571) rejects only footprint.len()<3, non-finite coords, and non-finite/negative height; it performs no simple-polygon or non-zero-area test, yet a DegenerateBuilding error variant already exists and is used for other degeneracies, so this is a real gap in that guard. is_convex (path.rs:203-224) only checks turn-sign consistency: I hand-verified the cited bowtie [[0,0],[10,10],[10,0],[0,10]] yields signs -1,-1,+1 → returns false → routes to concave_lateral_paths, and a collinear 3-vertex footprint short-circuits n<4→true → routes to the convex lateral_plane_hull; both mis-handle non-simple/degenerate input. barriers() (scene/mod.rs:631-643) copies the footprint verbatim into WallBarrier (over-top) and FootprintLateral (lateral) with no repair, so the wrong lateral energy-sums into Abar (barrier/mod.rs:96-114) and a spuriously short lateral under-predicts attenuation (non-conservative) with no error to the caller. It is non-crashing (polygon_interior_point returns None→empty for the bowtie; non-finite is already blocked so no NaN reaches the partial_cmp unwraps). Severity is correctly minor rather than major/critical: it needs malformed input (not a wrong result on valid scenes, not a panic). The claim is somewhat GIGO — a random self-intersecting building is unrealistic and the collinear sub-case degrades gracefully to a thin-wall screen — but a transposed-corner footprint (e.g. [[0,0],[10,0],[0,10],[10,10]], a plausible vertex-order data error) is a realistic trigger that silently produces a non-conservative barrier attenuation, which clears the minor bar for a robustness/misleading-behaviour defect.

confirmed.summary: cap() accepts the dz_cap_db override without bounding it to [0, standard], so a negative override yields negative (amplifying) barrier attenuation and an override above the ISO limit silently disables the 20/25 dB cap.
confirmed.detail: cap() computes `let max_db = override_cap_db.unwrap_or(20|25); if dz > max_db { max_db } else { dz }`. max_db is never bounded to a sane range. The value comes from Settings.dz_cap_db (Option<f64>) passed straight through the evaluator (standards/mod.rs:132 via GeneralEval.dz_cap; scene/mod.rs:919/947/998/1058/1100/1155). Scene::validate (scene/mod.rs:485-493) finiteness-checks c0_db but OMITS dz_cap_db, so any finite value — including negatives — passes validation and reaches cap(). Three failure modes: (a) Some(-3.0): cap returns -3.0; dz_top=-3, and in barrier/mod.rs the `lat_lengths.is_empty()` branch (line 103-104) returns `abar_top` with NO floor at 0, so Abar=-3 in every screened band; evaluate_general then does `- agr - abar` = `... + 3`, i.e. the obstacle ADDS 3 dB. (b) Some(30.0): over-top Dz capped at 30, exceeding ISO 9613-2 §7.4 / TR §5.3's 20 dB single- / 25 dB double-diffraction ceiling — silently non-conformant, contradicting the code's own 'tighter project-level cap' doc. (c) Some(NaN) via the typed/py API: `dz > NaN` is false so cap returns the raw uncapped dz. The wasm shim guards v>=0 (iso9613-wasm/src/lib.rs:60) but not the upper bound; the typed/JSON/py seams guard neither.
confirmed.failure_scenario: solve_json (or the typed Scene API) with `settings.dz_cap_db = -3.0` and a receiver shadowed by a terrain ridge (terrain edges emit no lateral edges, so BarrierGeometry.lateral is empty). abar_spectrum takes the no-lateral branch and emits Abar = -3 dB unfloored in every band the ridge screens; evaluate_general subtracts a negative, so the predicted Lp is 3 dB HIGHER with the hill than without it — a 'barrier' that amplifies. The same unbounded path lets dz_cap_db=30 push over-top Dz above the ISO 25 dB cap.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Bound the override in cap(), e.g. `let max_db = override_cap_db.map(|v| v.clamp(0.0, if e_total < 1e-9 {20.0} else {25.0})).unwrap_or(std_cap);` (and/or floor the emitted over-top Abar at 0 in barrier/mod.rs, and add a dz_cap_db range check to Scene::validate).

verdict.reasoning: Verified end-to-end and survives refutation. cap() (diffraction.rs:117-125) applies override_cap_db with no clamp: for Some(-3.0), max_db=-3 and dz>-3 holds for any dz>=0, so cap returns -3; for Some(NaN), `dz > NaN` is false so cap returns the raw uncapped dz (silently disabling the ISO cap). This override is a public serde field Settings.dz_cap_db (scene/mod.rs:258), deserialized by solve_json (scene/mod.rs:1231) and settable via the typed API/Session/py. Scene::validate (scene/mod.rs:485-491) finiteness-checks the adjacent c0_db but omits dz_cap_db, so negative/NaN values pass validation unchanged and reach cap() (flow: solve@847 -> GeneralEval.dz_cap@919 -> abar_spectrum standards/mod.rs:132). In abar_spectrum, a negative dz_top takes the else branch (barrier/mod.rs:92-94) giving abar_top<0, and the lat_lengths.is_empty() branch (line 103-104) returns it UNFLOORED — unlike the with-lateral branch which floors at 0 (line 113). evaluate_general then does `- abar` (standards/mod.rs:138), so a -3 dB Abar raises Lp by 3 dB: a barrier that amplifies. This no-lateral branch is realistically reachable because build_geometry routes terrain_edges into over_top only (path.rs:904,922) and never into lateral (926-931), so a terrain-ridge-screened receiver yields empty lateral. Three concrete internal inconsistencies confirm this is a genuine defect, not garbage-in/garbage-out: (1) validate() guards c0_db but not dz_cap_db; (2) the no-lateral branch omits the max(0.0) floor its with-lateral sibling applies (barrier/mod.rs:113); (3) the author's own wasm shim explicitly rejects negative/non-finite dz_cap (iso9613-wasm/src/lib.rs:59-61 with an explanatory comment), a contract the typed/JSON/py seams fail to honor. Severity is minor (matching the finding, not higher) because the wrong result is gated behind a misconfigured input a careful user would not supply; there is no panic (all outputs stay finite) and normal inputs (None or non-negative dz_cap_db) always yield Abar>=0.

confirmed.summary: adiv returns -inf when source and receiver coincide (d = 0), producing +inf per-band levels that serialize to JSON null and silently collapse total_dba to None.
confirmed.detail: Adiv = 20*log10(d) + 11 with d = 0 evaluates 20*log10(0) = -inf (no panic). In StandardModel::evaluate_general the band level is out = lw + d_corr - adiv - aatm - agr - abar, so -(-inf) makes every band +inf. serde_json encodes non-finite f64 as null, so SourceContribution.bands round-trips through solve_json as an array of nulls, while total_dba is guarded by is_finite() to None -- a value that normally signals 'no source contributes', masking the degenerate coincident-geometry input rather than surfacing it. No minimum-distance floor (d0 = 1 m) is applied before the log.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A Receiver whose position equals a Source position (or, less exactly, an area/line sub-source landing directly under a co-located receiver). solve()/solve_json then reports that source's bands as [null, null, ...] and total_dba as null with no error, silently dropping the loudest contribution instead of flagging it.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Clamp the distance before the logarithm, e.g. `let d = receiver_pos.sub(source_pos).length().max(1e-9);` (or reject/return a defined large value for d below a small threshold) so the output stays finite.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed and reachable. divergence.rs:15-16 computes 20.0*d.log10()+11.0 with no distance floor; for d=0, 0.0_f64.log10()=-inf (IEEE754, no panic), so adiv=-inf. At standards/mod.rs:138 the band level is lw + d_corr - adiv - aatm - agr - abar, and -(-inf) makes every band +inf (aatm=0 at d=0, agr/abar finite). This is reachable through the public API: Source.position:[f64;3] (scene/mod.rs:136) and Receiver.position:[f64;3] (:148) are free absolute coordinates, and solve_cached builds the slant distance directly from them (:880,:883) independent of height_agl; validate() (:496-536) checks only finiteness/structure and applies NO coincidence guard and NO minimum-distance floor (the 1e-9 clamps at :817/:824 are in the terrain horizontal-distance path, not the adiv slant path). Downstream, solve_json serializes via serde_json::to_string (:1233), which encodes non-finite f64 as JSON null, so SourceContribution.bands round-trips as [null, null, ...]; and total_dba's is_finite() guard (:1191) yields None. Per the ReceiverResult doc comment (:424) None is documented to mean 'no source contributes (-inf)' i.e. silence, so the degenerate coincident-geometry case (the loudest input in this far-field model) is silently reported as if it were total silence, with no error. Not an ISO misread: the code correctly implements 20*log10(d/d0)+11 with d0=1; this is a pure robustness/degenerate-input defect. Severity minor rather than major: it requires a physically meaningless exact float-coincidence (measure-zero; a correct host would never co-locate receiver and source), the effect is contained to that one source-receiver pair without corrupting valid results, there is no panic, and the output is a visibly anomalous null rather than a believable wrong number.

confirmed.summary: fresnel_valid's vertical foreshortening uses the ray elevation angle (cos_ah = sp_horiz/sp_len) instead of Eq 27's alpha_h, the angle of incidence projected onto the vertical plane perpendicular to the facade.
confirmed.detail: Eq 27 defines alpha_h as the incidence angle projected onto a vertical plane RECTANGULAR to the reflecting surface, i.e. cos alpha_h = |n_component| / sqrt(n_component^2 + z^2), where n_component is the ray's plan component along the facade normal. That projection must exclude the along-facade (tangential) component. The code instead uses cos_ah = sp_horiz/sp_len = sqrt(u^2+n^2)/sqrt(u^2+n^2+z^2), which includes the along-facade component u. Algebraically code_cos^2 - standard_cos^2 = u^2·z^2 / ((u^2+n^2)(n^2+z^2)) >= 0, so the code's cos_ah is always >= the standard's, making leff larger and the gate strictly more permissive (one-directional over-inclusion of reflections). The horizontal term cos_aa (line 315) is computed correctly. The common case (tall facades where the horizontal term binds, or near-normal incidence where u≈0) is unaffected, which is why T19 passed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A short reflector (e.g. a 2 m acoustic barrier reused as a reflector, base_z=0/top_z=2) with source and receiver at noticeably different heights (steep ray, z large) and offset so the reflection is oblique in plan (u comparable to n). Here the vertical term h·cos_ah binds and the code overestimates it, so high-frequency bands that the standard's alpha_h would reject via Eq 26 are passed, adding spurious reflected energy and over-predicting the level.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED. ISO 9613-2:2024 (ref text line 1365) defines Eq 27's α_h as "the angle of incidence projected to a vertical plane rectangular to the reflecting surface." For a vertical facade with plan-normal n̂ and horizontal tangent ŵ, that vertical plane is spanned by n̂ and ẑ, so projecting the ray discards the along-facade component u, giving cos α_h = |n|/√(n²+z²). reflection.rs:313 instead computes cos_ah = sp_horiz/sp_len = √(u²+n²)/√(u²+n²+z²), the true 3-D elevation angle, which retains u. Since x/(x+z²) is increasing, cos_ah(code) ≥ cos α_h(std) always (equality only at u=0), so h·cos_ah is over-estimated; when the vertical term is the binding min in leff=min(a·cos_aa, h·cos_ah) (line 316), leff is too large, Eq 26 (line 320) becomes strictly more permissive, and reflected bands the standard rejects are admitted. The horizontal term cos_aa (line 315 = |n|/√(u²+n²)) is correct. Worked example (x-aligned facade, h=2 m, ray (u,n,z)=(10,5,8), wide facade, dSO=dOR=20 m): code cos_ah=0.813→leff=1.63 admits 4 kHz; standard cos α_h=0.530→leff=1.06 rejects it, so the code energy-sums a spurious reflected contribution. Reachable: fresnel_valid gates the first-order reflected energy into output bands at scene/mod.rs:1004, and Reflector.base_z/top_z (scene/mod.rs:280-281) are public with no min-height validation, so a short 2 m reflector with a steep plan-oblique ray is constructible via the typed/JSON API. T19 passing does not exonerate it because that case has a tall facade / near-normal incidence (u≈0). Severity minor: the deviation is one-directional over-inclusion, but it only activates when the vertical term binds (short/wide reflectors; tall facades make the horizontal term bind and the bug inert), the ray is plan-oblique, and steep — and the over-included energy is confined to the top one or two octave bands, giving a sub-dB effect on the A-weighted total in narrow geometry.

confirmed.summary: Chimney Dc is interpolated linearly in ka, but Annex B Formula (B.4) specifies logarithmic interpolation (x = (ln ka - ln ka1)/(ln ka2 - ln ka1)).
confirmed.detail: `chimney_dc` calls `interp(&KA, &DC[ti], ka)` (line 47), and `interp` interpolates linearly in ka. Formula (B.4) mandates interpolation in ln(ka). Because the ka grid is geometric (4·2^(n/3), ratio ~1.26) the in-range error is small (<~0.02 dB). The larger deviation is in the 1<ka<4 extension (line 53), which uses linear (ka-1)/3 rather than ln(ka)/ln(4): at ka=2 (θ=45°) this gives Dc=1.33 dB vs 2.0 dB logarithmic — a ~0.5-0.7 dB error. ka≈2 corresponds to ~63 Hz for a 2 m opening, so for low-frequency-dominated industrial stacks this shifts the low octaves, though A-weighting attenuates the effect on the total.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A ChimneyStack source with opening_radius ~2 m evaluated at 63 Hz where ka lands near 2: the returned Dc is ~0.5-0.7 dB below the standard's logarithmic value, biasing the modelled 63 Hz emission (and any low-frequency limit assessment) low.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed, with independent reproduction against the standard's own worked example. ISO 9613-2:2024 Formula (B.4) (iso2024.txt:2135) specifies the ka interpolation weight as x = (ln ka − ln ka1)/(ln ka2 − ln ka1), i.e. logarithmic in ka. The code interpolates linearly in ka in both regimes: annex_b.rs:48 calls the linear `interp` (annex_b.rs:25-40) on the raw KA grid, and annex_b.rs:53 uses (ka−1.0)/3.0·DC[ti][0] for the 1<ka<4 extension. The in-range deviation (4≤ka≤32) is negligible (<~0.03 dB) because the ka grid is geometric, but the extension deviation is real and reproduces a concrete disagreement with the standard: Table B.2/B.3 Example 1 (opening radius a=2 m, relevant angle θ=105.8°) gives ka=2.02 and Dc=−2.2 dB at 63 Hz. Applying B.4 (x=ln2.02/ln4=0.507, y=0.0533) yields −2.24≈−2.2 dB, matching Table B.3 exactly; the code's linear branch (x=(2.02−1)/3=0.34) yields −1.50 dB — a 0.7 dB error at 63 Hz for the standard's own example. The path is reachable via the public API (scene/mod.rs:928-939, SourceKind::ChimneyStack; ka built from band centre + opening_radius_m + temperature with no radius validation), and a 2 m opening radius is exactly the standard's Example 1, not an exotic input. The unit test at annex_b.rs:103 pins the linear value, confirming the behavior is deliberate and unguarded. Severity is minor rather than major because the large error is confined to the 1<ka<4 low-frequency extension (an extrapolation the standard itself flags as beyond its 4≤ka≤32 measurement basis), and 63 Hz A-weighting (−26 dB) makes the effect on the A-weighted total — the primary assessed output and what the conformance suite checks — negligible; only the per-band low-frequency value for large industrial stacks is visibly wrong.

confirmed.summary: Reflector/cylinder absorption and radius are not validated; a negative alpha yields 10·lg(1-alpha) > 0 — an image source LOUDER than the real source (physical gain).
confirmed.detail: `validate()` (lines 477-587) checks sources, receivers and obstacles but never checks `reflectors`, `cylinders`, `amisc`, or `ChimneyStack.opening_radius_m`. The reflection-loss guard `(1.0 - alpha).max(1e-12).log10()` (lines 984, 1046, 1091) only defends against alpha>=1; for alpha<0 it evaluates 10·lg(1-alpha) to a POSITIVE value, so a negative absorption coefficient silently amplifies the reflected image source instead of attenuating it. Separately, `validate()` does not enforce cylinder radius>0: in reflect_cylinder (line 241) `d/cyl.radius` with radius=0 gives k that drives Acurv to +inf (reflection silently vanishes), and radius<0 can make (1-k^2) negative -> powf(-0.5) NaN -> the whole receiver total_dba becomes None via the is_finite guard.

A CylindricalReflector with radius=0 or radius<0 either silently contributes nothing or forces the receiver's total_dba to None (no result reported).

verdict.reasoning: Core finding verified. Consequently alpha=-0.2 via solve_json passes validation and at lines 984/1046/1091 the guard `(1.0 - alpha).max(1e-12).log10()` — which only defends alpha>=1 — yields 10*lg(1.2) = +0.79 dB, an image source LOUDER than a perfect mirror, silently energy-summed (and compounding per bounce in the higher-order chain at line 1046); unbounded for more-negative alpha. rejected.summary: The concave homotopy cut ray uses a fixed slope (0.0007) from a deterministic interior point; if it aligns with a footprint vertex / graph-edge endpoint, parity flips are miscounted and the two lateral wraps merge or duplicate.
rejected.refutation: The mechanism the finding describes is technically real: `crosses_cut` (path.rs:534-545) counts a cut-ray crossing only for strict interior segment parameter `sp ∈ (1e-9, 1−1e-9)`, so a footprint vertex lying exactly on the cut ray `interior + u·(1, 0.0007)` makes both incident edges non-crossing at that node and can drop one parity flip, corrupting the homotopy label. I independently re-derived the sp/t solve and it is correct, so the endpoint-exclusion behaviour is as claimed. However, the consequence is measure-zero and does not arise in realistic scenes, so it fails even the "minor = practical impact" bar. (1) The off-axis slope 0.0007 (path.rs:533) is deliberately chosen to dodge exactly the realistic degeneracies: axis-aligned vertices give slope 0 (off the ray), and the den-near-zero guard (path.rs:539) only fires for edges whose own slope is ≈0.0007 — never horizontal/vertical footprint edges. (2) All near-alignments are scored correctly; only an exact sub-1e-9 fractional graze (≈ edge_len·1e-9, i.e. sub-micron) breaks, which for round-number L/U-shape coordinates against their rational centroid (path.rs:472-497) never occurs by accident — it requires an adversarially tuned footprint satisfying v.y−i.y = 0.0007·(v.x−i.x) exactly. (3) Even then a wrong Abar additionally requires an *optimal* wrap to route through the exact grazing vertex; otherwise the shortest parity-0/parity-1 paths at R are scored correctly. The passing T18 conformance case confirms the generic parity/branch-cut technique is sound. This is a legitimate but purely theoretical robustness nit (refutation angle d: measure-zero geometry), not a defect that produces wrong results in any plausible user-supplied concave building.

infoNotes.summary: lateral_path_lengths doc claims delta_z <= 0 'when the edge doesn't shadow the receiver', but delta_z = ls+lr-d_direct >= 0 always (triangle inequality); the described 'reads as Dz=0, fully open' branch never triggers.
infoNotes.detail: ls and lr are the true 3-D distances S->P and P->R for P on the vertical end-edge, so ls+lr >= |S-R| = d_direct with equality only when P lies on the segment; delta_z is never negative. The comment (lines 96-99) misdescribes the behaviour: a lateral around a wall end always yields Dz >= 10*lg(3) ~= 4.8 dB (the standard finite-barrier floor from dz_uncapped_lateral, since delta_z >= 0 > z_min), never a fully-open Dz=0. The code is correct; only the comment is misleading and could invite a wrong 'open path' assumption in future edits.
infoNotes.failure_scenario: No runtime failure - documentation defect only. A maintainer relying on the comment might add an `if delta_z <= 0 { open }` shortcut expecting it to fire for non-shadowing ends; it never would, and removing the ~4.8 dB floor would then mis-model finite barriers.
infoNotes.fix_sketch: Correct the comment to state delta_z >= 0 always and that a lateral end path carries the standard >=~4.8 dB minimum, not a Dz=0 open path.

infoNotes.summary: ChimneyStack computes ka with the ambient atmosphere temperature, but annex_b::ka's contract (and Annex B.3) specify the chimney-mouth temperature; the scene exposes no mouth temperature.
infoNotes.detail: Line 937 calls annex_b::ka(*opening_radius_m, f, atm.temperature_c) using ambient air temperature for the speed of sound c = 331.4*sqrt(1+T/273). annex_b::ka's own doc (annex_b.rs 76-79) says c is 'at the chimney-mouth temperature T'. Since a hot flue has a higher c (larger wavelength, smaller ka), the Table B.1 Dc interpolation over ka is biased. There is no mouth-temperature field on SourceKind::ChimneyStack, so ambient is the only value available.
infoNotes.failure_scenario: A stack emitting at e.g. 150 C mouth temperature vs 10 C ambient: true c is ~15% higher, so true ka is ~15% lower, shifting the interpolated Dc; the solver silently uses the ambient-based ka. Small but the doc and code disagree on which temperature applies.
infoNotes.fix_sketch: Add an optional mouth-temperature to ChimneyStack and pass it to ka, or correct the annex_b::ka doc to state ambient temperature is used.

infoNotes.summary: WindTurbine sources pass the uniform scene.ground.default_g to evaluate_wtg and ignore ground-cover regions, whereas General and ChimneyStack sources use per-region g_source/g_middle/g_receiver.
infoNotes.detail: At line 924 the WTG arm passes `g` (= scene.ground.default_g, bound at line 864), not the region_ground_factors triple that is computed (885-892) and used by the General/Chimney arms. evaluate_wtg then applies a single G (capped to 0.5). So a scene with GroundRegions silently applies uniform default_g to WTG paths. This may be intended given Annex D.4's G<=0.5 simplification, but it is undocumented and inconsistent with the other source kinds.
infoNotes.failure_scenario: A turbine over farmland with a modelled hard-standing GroundRegion (g=0) under/near it: General sources would see the region in their source-region G, but the WTG source uses default_g everywhere, so its Agr ignores the hard standing — a silent per-source inconsistency.
infoNotes.fix_sketch: Compute per-region factors for WTG as well (still capping each at 0.5), or document that WTG uses uniform default_g by design.

infoNotes.summary: Core scalar/vec fields (Settings.c0_db, Scene.sources/receivers/obstacles/settings) lack #[serde(default)] while the newer optional vecs have it, so a minimal/partial scene JSON fails to parse.
infoNotes.detail: The newer fields (terrain, extended_sources, reflectors, cylinders, amisc, ground.regions, Wall.top_z, ground_method, max_reflection_order) all carry #[serde(default)], but c0_db is a required f64 and sources/receivers/obstacles/settings are required with no default. The seam is JSON in/out for FFI (py, wasm/C hosts), so producers hand-building scenes hit surprising 'missing field' errors on otherwise-valid partial input. This is an ergonomics/consistency gap, not a forward-compat regression (these fields predate the defaulted ones).
infoNotes.failure_scenario: A producer serialises a scene with "settings": {} (meaning 'all default settings') -> serde_json fails with 'missing field `c0_db`'. Omitting an empty "obstacles":[] -> 'missing field `obstacles`', even though omitting "reflectors" is fine. The inconsistency is easy to trip over on the JSON boundary.
infoNotes.fix_sketch: Add #[serde(default)] to c0_db and (if a bare scene should parse) to sources/receivers/obstacles/settings, so a partial scene fills in defaults consistently.

infoNotes.summary: An extended source with too few geometry vertices is reported as SceneError::BadLwLength, whose message talks about sound-power band count, misdirecting the fault.
infoNotes.detail: The min-vertex check for line/area geometry reuses BadLwLength { source_id, len: verts.len() } (line 517). Its Display (line 451-453) renders 'source X: lw has 2 bands (expected 10 octave or 31 third-octave)' when the actual problem is the polygon/polyline vertex count, not lw. Consumers keying on the error variant or text will point users at the wrong field.
infoNotes.failure_scenario: ExtendedSource with ExtentGeometry::Area{ polygon: [[0,0],[1,0]] } (2 vertices) and a valid 10-band lw fails with SceneError::BadLwLength{len:2}; a UI surfacing that error tells the user their sound power spectrum is the wrong length, when the fault is the 2-vertex area polygon.
infoNotes.fix_sketch: Introduce a dedicated variant (e.g. DegenerateExtendedSource { id, reason }) for the geometry vertex-count check instead of overloading BadLwLength.

infoNotes.summary: T16 test comment cites the wrong TR table for the reference values.
infoNotes.detail: The comment says "Table 52 (the unweighted L row + 32.54 total)". In the TR, Table 52 is the single-number ground-properties table (Gs/Gr/Gm); the unweighted L row [41.03, 34.28, 29.33, 26.64, 26.45, 25.68, 24.22, 21.07] and the 32.54 LAa total that the test asserts come from Table 54 ("Spectral step by step results (T16)"). The asserted numbers are correct (verified against the TR) — only the table citation is wrong, which slightly weakens traceability of the reference.
infoNotes.failure_scenario: A reviewer cross-checking the t16 reference opens TR Table 52, finds ground factors instead of the L row, and cannot confirm the transcription without hunting for the right table.
infoNotes.fix_sketch: Change "Table 52" to "Table 54" in the t16 comment (line 368).
